# Roots grow from their tips

<!-- STEP id="tips" -->
## Growth happens at the tip

Cutting off just 1 cm stopped the roots from growing, so the growth of a root must happen at its tip. **Roots grow only from their tips**, because the tips have cells that divide again and again.

<!-- STEP id="mitosis" -->
## You have seen these cells before

In an earlier chapter, on cells, you may have seen cells dividing by mitosis in an onion root tip under a microscope. That observation agrees with this experiment: root tips contain actively dividing cells.

<!-- STEP id="shoot-tips" -->
## Shoot tips too

Shoot tips also have actively dividing cells, which make the shoot grow taller. These growth zones at the tips of roots and shoots are called **apical meristems**, because apical means at the tip, or apex.

**Apical meristems at the tips of roots and shoots make a plant grow in length.**
